about: How a body is posed, from V1 characters.ts (RPG-game trunk 82a994d15). No crossfades: every clip plays all the time and its weight eases toward a target. Locomotion blends idle, walk, the two strafes and run by the smoothed travel speed; the combat clip's target weight rises over `blendMs.<kind>.in` after the move starts and falls over `.out` before it ends, snapping to full through the blade's active ticks. All blends are in milliseconds (A1, Strategy 26 Oct: none above 150): `locomotion` is the time an eased weight takes to close ~95 % of its gap (V1's weightRate 24/s is 125 ms); attack, special and hurt rows replace V1's fadeIn 12 / fadeOut 10 (fractions of the move: about 75 / 80 ms on a 0.83 s swing, now fixed whatever the move's length). `settleMs` is the one named exception to the 150 cap: a roll-to-run ends in a run pose, so the roll's weight eases out over 300 ms and the run-out blends into the stance instead of snapping (Dom 26 Oct). Swings are scrubbed by sim progress through the keys below (a slow wind-up, a snap through contact, a slow tail) instead of played at a constant rate.
